# # Dependency Trace: S3 Multipart Upload from boto3 through s3transfer to botocore

## Context

When uploading large files to S3 with boto3, the actual work is split across
three libraries: boto3 provides the high-level API, s3transfer handles
multipart upload orchestration (splitting, concurrency, completion), and
botocore provides the low-level AWS API calls with serialization and retries.

A timeout issue with large uploads requires understanding how configuration
flows through all three layers.

## Task

Trace a single `upload_file` call from boto3's S3 resource through s3transfer's
multipart upload logic to botocore's API call serialization. Document
configuration options at each layer.

## Repos in Workspace

- `/workspace/boto3/` -- boto3 1.28.0 (high-level SDK)
- `/workspace/s3transfer/` -- s3transfer 0.6.1 (transfer orchestration)
- `/workspace/botocore/` -- botocore 1.31.0 (low-level API client)

## Expected Output

Write `/workspace/DEPENDENCY_TRACE.md` containing:

1. boto3's upload_file entry point and TransferConfig options
2. s3transfer's TransferManager multipart upload orchestration
3. botocore's low-level S3 operations (CreateMultipartUpload, UploadPart, CompleteMultipartUpload)
4. Configuration options at each layer that affect upload behavior
5. The complete call chain from upload_file to HTTP requests


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/boto3--1.28.0, github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1, github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0

# Dependency Trace: S3 Multipart Upload

`boto3 1.28.0` → `s3transfer 0.6.1` → `botocore 1.31.0`

## 1. boto3 Layer — Entry Point and TransferConfig

### Entry Point: `upload_file`

boto3 injects `upload_file` onto three surfaces (S3 client, Bucket resource, Object resource) via
[`boto3/s3/inject.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/boto3--1.28.0/-/blob/boto3/s3/inject.py?L105-149).
All three ultimately call the same code path:

```python
# boto3/s3/inject.py  L105-149
def upload_file(self, Filename, Bucket, Key,
                ExtraArgs=None, Callback=None, Config=None):
    with S3Transfer(self, Config) as transfer:
        return transfer.upload_file(
            filename=Filename, bucket=Bucket, key=Key,
            extra_args=ExtraArgs, callback=Callback)
```

[`S3Transfer.__init__`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/boto3--1.28.0/-/blob/boto3/s3/transfer.py?L250-268)
calls `create_transfer_manager(client, config)` which returns an
`s3transfer.manager.TransferManager`. If `config.use_threads` is `False`,
`NonThreadedExecutor` is passed to the manager so that all logic runs on the main thread
([`transfer.py` L158-161](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/boto3--1.28.0/-/blob/boto3/s3/transfer.py?L158-161)).

[`S3Transfer.upload_file`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/boto3--1.28.0/-/blob/boto3/s3/transfer.py?L270-292)
wraps the filename check, builds a subscriber list from the optional `Callback`, then delegates:

```python
future = self._manager.upload(filename, bucket, key, extra_args, subscribers)
future.result()   # blocks until complete; raises S3UploadFailedError on failure
```

### boto3 TransferConfig ([`boto3/s3/transfer.py` L164-235](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/boto3--1.28.0/-/blob/boto3/s3/transfer.py?L164-235))

`boto3.s3.transfer.TransferConfig` subclasses `s3transfer.manager.TransferConfig`, adding two
aliases and the `use_threads` flag.

| boto3 parameter        | s3transfer attribute       | Default | Effect                                                  |
|------------------------|----------------------------|---------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| `multipart_threshold`  | `multipart_threshold`      | 8 MB    | File size above which multipart upload is used          |
| `multipart_chunksize`  | `multipart_chunksize`      | 8 MB    | Size of each individual part                            |
| `max_concurrency`      | `max_request_concurrency`  | 10      | Max concurrent S3 API threads                           |
| `max_io_queue`         | `max_io_queue_size`        | 100     | Max read parts buffered in memory (downloads)           |
| `io_chunksize`         | `io_chunksize`             | 256 KB  | Size of each `read()` chunk from the source file        |
| `num_download_attempts`| `num_download_attempts`    | 5       | Streaming-error retries for downloads only              |
| `max_bandwidth`        | `max_bandwidth`            | None    | Bytes-per-second cap on upload/download throughput      |
| `use_threads`          | _(boto3-only)_             | `True`  | `False` → `NonThreadedExecutor`, single-threaded uploads|

### Allowed ExtraArgs for Upload ([`s3transfer/manager.py` L159-187](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/manager.py?L159-187))

## 2. s3transfer Layer — TransferManager Multipart Orchestration

### TransferManager Construction ([`s3transfer/manager.py` L217-281](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/manager.py?L217-281))

`TransferManager.__init__` creates three thread pools driven by `TransferConfig`:

| Executor               | Threads                          | Queue size                        | Role                                          |
|------------------------|----------------------------------|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `_request_executor`    | `max_request_concurrency` (10)   | `max_request_queue_size` (1000)   | Makes all S3 API calls (Create/Upload/Complete)|
| `_submission_executor` | `max_submission_concurrency` (5) | `max_submission_queue_size` (1000)| Determines upload strategy, submits tasks     |
| `_io_executor`         | 1 (fixed)                        | `max_io_queue_size` (1000)        | Disk I/O for downloads                        |

If `max_bandwidth` is set, a `BandwidthLimiter` backed by a `LeakyBucket` token-rate throttler
is created and passed to upload tasks ([`manager.py` L274-279](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/manager.py?L274-279)).

Memory ceiling for file-object uploads ([`manager.py` L110-113](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/manager.py?L110-113)):
```
max_in_memory_upload_chunks × multipart_chunksize
  + max_submission_concurrency × multipart_chunksize
```

### TransferManager.upload() ([`manager.py` L291-335](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/manager.py?L291-335))

```python
def upload(self, fileobj, bucket, key, extra_args=None, subscribers=None):
    call_args = CallArgs(fileobj=fileobj, bucket=bucket, key=key,
                         extra_args=extra_args, subscribers=subscribers)
    return self._submit_transfer(call_args, UploadSubmissionTask, extra_main_kwargs)
```

Wraps everything in a `TransferFuture`, submits `UploadSubmissionTask` to `_submission_executor`,
and returns the future immediately (non-blocking).

### UploadSubmissionTask._submit() ([`upload.py` L552-607](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/upload.py?L552-607))

1. **Selects input manager** by probing the `fileobj` type:
   - `UploadFilenameInputManager` — string file paths (`os.stat` for size)
   - `UploadSeekableInputManager` — seekable file-like objects
   - `UploadNonSeekableInputManager` — non-seekable streams (buffers up to threshold to decide)

2. **Determines upload strategy** via `requires_multipart_upload(transfer_future, config)`:
   - If `transfer_future.meta.size >= config.multipart_threshold` → multipart
   - For non-seekable streams: reads up to `threshold` bytes; `len(data) < threshold` → single `PutObject`

3. Dispatches to `_submit_upload_request` (single PUT) or `_submit_multipart_request`.

### Multipart Upload Path ([`upload.py` L644-728](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/upload.py?L644-728))

**Step 1 — CreateMultipartUpload** — submitted first; all part tasks depend on its `upload_id`:

```python
# tasks.py L337-360
response = client.create_multipart_upload(Bucket=bucket, Key=key, **extra_args)
upload_id = response['UploadId']
# Registers abort_multipart_upload as failure cleanup
self._transfer_coordinator.add_failure_cleanup(
    client.abort_multipart_upload, Bucket=bucket, Key=key, UploadId=upload_id)
```

**Step 2 — ChunksizeAdjuster** enforces S3 constraints ([`utils.py` L28-33](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/utils.py?L28-33)):
- Minimum part size: **5 MB** (`MIN_UPLOAD_CHUNKSIZE`)
- Maximum parts: **10,000** (`MAX_PARTS`)
- Maximum total upload: **5 GB** (`MAX_SINGLE_UPLOAD_SIZE`)

**Step 3 — UploadPartTask** per part (concurrent, bounded by `max_request_concurrency`):

```python
# upload.py L764-795
response = client.upload_part(
    Bucket=bucket, Key=key,
    UploadId=upload_id, PartNumber=part_number,
    Body=body, **extra_part_args)
# Returns {'ETag': etag, 'PartNumber': part_number}
```

Extra args forwarded to `upload_part` ([`UPLOAD_PART_ARGS`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/upload.py?L515-522)):
`ChecksumAlgorithm`, `SSECustomerKey`, `SSECustomerAlgorithm`, `SSECustomerKeyMD5`,
`RequestPayer`, `ExpectedBucketOwner`

**Step 4 — CompleteMultipartUpload** — `is_final=True`, waits for all parts:

```python
# tasks.py L381-387
client.complete_multipart_upload(
    Bucket=bucket, Key=key, UploadId=upload_id,
    MultipartUpload={'Parts': parts},   # [{ETag, PartNumber}, ...]
    **extra_args)
```

Extra args forwarded to `complete_multipart_upload` ([`COMPLETE_MULTIPART_ARGS`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/upload.py?L524)):
`RequestPayer`, `ExpectedBucketOwner`

### s3transfer TransferConfig Reference ([`manager.py` L46-153](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/manager.py?L46-153))

| Parameter                     | Default | Effect                                                       |
|-------------------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `multipart_threshold`         | 8 MB    | Threshold for choosing multipart vs. PutObject               |
| `multipart_chunksize`         | 8 MB    | Target part size (auto-adjusted to S3 constraints)           |
| `max_request_concurrency`     | 10      | Threads making S3 API requests                               |
| `max_submission_concurrency`  | 5       | Threads deciding upload strategy / submitting tasks          |
| `max_request_queue_size`      | 1000    | Max queued S3 API tasks (back-pressure)                      |
| `max_submission_queue_size`   | 1000    | Max queued submission tasks                                  |
| `max_io_queue_size`           | 1000    | Max queued disk-write chunks (downloads)                     |
| `io_chunksize`                | 256 KB  | `read()` chunk size from source stream                       |
| `num_download_attempts`       | 5       | Streaming-error retries for downloads                        |
| `max_in_memory_upload_chunks` | 10      | Semaphore on in-memory chunks for non-file-object uploads    |
| `max_bandwidth`               | None    | Bytes/sec cap via LeakyBucket token rate limiter             |

## 3. botocore Layer — Low-Level S3 API Calls

### _make_api_call() ([`botocore/client.py` L906-978](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/client.py?L906-978))

Every botocore S3 operation goes through this single entry point:

```
_make_api_call(operation_name, api_params)
  ├── operation_model = service_model.operation_model(operation_name)
  ├── _emit_api_params()              # fires provide-client-params + before-parameter-build events
  ├── _resolve_endpoint_ruleset()     # resolves endpoint URL via endpoint rules engine
  ├── _convert_to_request_dict()      # [client.py L994] serializes params → HTTP dict
  │     └── RestXMLSerializer.serialize_to_request(api_params, operation_model)
  │     └── prepare_request_dict()    # attach endpoint URL + User-Agent
  ├── resolve_checksum_context()      # CRC32/SHA256 header injection
  ├── emit before-call event          # SigV4 request signing
  ├── apply_request_checksum()
  └── _make_request()                 # → endpoint.make_request()
        └── _send_request()           # retry loop + HTTP send
```

### Request Serialization ([`botocore/serialize.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/serialize.py?L83-119))

S3 uses the `rest-xml` protocol. `serialize_to_request()` returns:

```python
{
    'url_path': '/bucket/key?uploadId=...',
    'query_string': 'partNumber=1&uploadId=...',
    'method': 'PUT',
    'headers': {'Content-Length': '...', 'x-amz-server-side-encryption': '...'},
    'body': <file-like object or bytes>,
}
```

### S3 Multipart Operation HTTP Mapping ([`service-2.json`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/data/s3/2006-03-01/service-2.json))

| Operation                  | HTTP   | URI                                  |
|----------------------------|--------|--------------------------------------|
| `CreateMultipartUpload`    | POST   | `/{Bucket}/{Key}?uploads`            |
| `UploadPart`               | PUT    | `/{Bucket}/{Key}?partNumber&uploadId`|
| `CompleteMultipartUpload`  | POST   | `/{Bucket}/{Key}?uploadId`           |
| `AbortMultipartUpload`     | DELETE | `/{Bucket}/{Key}?uploadId`           |
| `PutObject` (single-part)  | PUT    | `/{Bucket}/{Key}`                    |

### Retry Loop ([`endpoint.py` L194-233](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/endpoint.py?L194-233))

```python
attempts = 1
request = create_request(request_dict, operation_model)  # sign request
success_response, exception = _get_response(request, ...)
while _needs_retry(attempts, operation_model, ...):
    attempts += 1
    request.reset_stream()       # rewind Body for retry
    request = create_request(...)  # re-sign with new timestamp
    success_response, exception = _get_response(request, ...)
```

`_needs_retry` fires `needs-retry.s3.<OperationName>`; registered handlers return a sleep
duration or `None`. urllib3-level retries are disabled (`retries=Retry(False)`).

### HTTP Execution ([`httpsession.py` L448-503](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/httpsession.py?L448-503))

```python
urllib_response = conn.urlopen(
    method=request.method,
    url=request_target,
    body=request.body,
    headers=request.headers,
    retries=Retry(False),       # urllib3 retries disabled; botocore owns the loop
    chunked=self._chunked(request.headers),
)
```

Timeout flow: `botocore.config.Config(connect_timeout, read_timeout)`
→ `EndpointCreator.create_endpoint(timeout=(connect, read))` ([`endpoint.py` L384-425](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/endpoint.py?L384-425))
→ `URLLib3Session(timeout=...)` ([`httpsession.py` L287-317](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/httpsession.py?L287-317))
→ `urllib3.Timeout(connect=..., read=...)` on every `urlopen()`.

### botocore Config Reference ([`botocore/config.py` L25-235](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/config.py?L25-235))

| Config parameter               | Default  | Effect on upload                                                    |
|--------------------------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `connect_timeout`              | 60 s     | TCP connection establishment timeout per attempt                    |
| `read_timeout`                 | 60 s     | **Critical for large uploads**: socket read idle timeout; if S3 takes longer than this to acknowledge a part, `ReadTimeoutError` is raised |
| `max_pool_connections`         | 10       | urllib3 pool size; should match `max_concurrency`                   |
| `retries['mode']`              | `legacy` | `legacy` / `standard` / `adaptive` — controls retry policy         |
| `retries['max_attempts']`      | 4 retries| Max retry attempts for throttling/5xx errors                        |
| `retries['total_max_attempts']`| —        | Total attempts including first; overrides `max_attempts`            |
| `s3['payload_signing_enabled']`| `False` (streaming) | SigV4 payload signing for UploadPart/PutObject          |
| `s3['addressing_style']`       | `auto`   | `virtual` / `path` — affects endpoint URL construction              |

## 5. Configuration for Timeout Issues with Large Uploads

The most common cause of large-upload failures is **`read_timeout`** (default **60 s** in
botocore). Each `UploadPart` request must fully complete within this window. With a slow
connection and the default 8 MB `multipart_chunksize`, a single part can easily exceed 60 s,
raising `ReadTimeoutError`. Botocore retries, but when retries are exhausted, s3transfer
automatically calls `abort_multipart_upload` via its registered failure cleanup.

```python
import boto3
from botocore.config import Config
from boto3.s3.transfer import TransferConfig

botocore_config = Config(
    read_timeout=300,           # 5 min per-part timeout
    connect_timeout=10,
    retries={'max_attempts': 3, 'mode': 'standard'},
    max_pool_connections=20,    # match max_concurrency
)
s3_client = boto3.client('s3', config=botocore_config)

transfer_config = TransferConfig(
    multipart_threshold=16 * 1024 * 1024,  # 16 MB
    multipart_chunksize=16 * 1024 * 1024,  # 16 MB parts
    max_concurrency=5,                      # fewer concurrent parts on slow links
    max_bandwidth=50 * 1024 * 1024,        # 50 MB/s optional cap
)

s3_client.upload_file('large_file.bin', 'mybucket', 'mykey', Config=transfer_config)
```

### Full Configuration Cross-Reference

| Concern                      | Layer            | Parameter                                          | Default    |
|------------------------------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------|------------|
| Multipart threshold          | boto3/s3transfer | `multipart_threshold`                              | 8 MB       |
| Part size                    | boto3/s3transfer | `multipart_chunksize`                              | 8 MB       |
| Concurrent part uploads      | boto3/s3transfer | `max_concurrency`                                  | 10         |
| Bandwidth cap                | boto3/s3transfer | `max_bandwidth`                                    | None       |
| Single-threaded mode         | boto3            | `use_threads=False`                                | `True`     |
| In-memory buffer limit       | s3transfer       | `max_in_memory_upload_chunks`                      | 10         |
| Submission threads           | s3transfer       | `max_submission_concurrency`                       | 5          |
| Per-request read timeout     | botocore         | `Config(read_timeout=...)`                         | 60 s       |
| Per-request connect timeout  | botocore         | `Config(connect_timeout=...)`                      | 60 s       |

The document above is `/workspace/DEPENDENCY_TRACE.md`. Here is a summary of each section:

**Section 1 — boto3 entry point.** [`upload_file`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/boto3--1.28.0/-/blob/boto3/s3/inject.py?L105-149) is injected onto the S3 client, Bucket, and Object surfaces. It constructs an [`S3Transfer`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/boto3--1.28.0/-/blob/boto3/s3/transfer.py?L246-292) which creates an `s3transfer.manager.TransferManager`, then calls `transfer.upload_file` which calls `manager.upload()` and blocks on `future.result()`. The boto3 [`TransferConfig`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/boto3--1.28.0/-/blob/boto3/s3/transfer.py?L164-235) wraps s3transfer's config and adds `use_threads`.

**Section 2 — s3transfer orchestration.** [`TransferManager`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/manager.py?L217-281) spins up three `BoundedExecutor` thread pools. [`UploadSubmissionTask`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/upload.py?L512-607) selects an input manager, checks the multipart threshold, and either submits a single `PutObjectTask` or a sequenced chain of [`CreateMultipartUploadTask`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/tasks.py?L334-360) → concurrent [`UploadPartTask`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/upload.py?L761-805)s → [`CompleteMultipartUploadTask`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/s3transfer--0.6.1/-/blob/s3transfer/tasks.py?L363-387). Failure at any point triggers registered `abort_multipart_upload` cleanup.

**Section 3 — botocore low-level calls.** Every botocore S3 call goes through [`_make_api_call`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/client.py?L906-978): serialize via `RestXMLSerializer`, SigV4 sign, then enter [`Endpoint._send_request`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/endpoint.py?L194-233) which runs the retry loop. The actual HTTP send is [`URLLib3Session.send`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/httpsession.py?L448-503) → `urllib3.conn.urlopen()`.

**Key timeout finding:** `read_timeout` (default 60 s, [`botocore/config.py` L219](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/botocore--1.31.0/-/blob/botocore/config.py?L219)) is applied per HTTP request via `urllib3.Timeout`. For large parts over slow connections this must be increased (e.g. `Config(read_timeout=300)`). Reduce `multipart_chunksize` to keep individual part transfer times under the timeout, or increase `read_timeout` directly.
